name: Augustine
dossier: North African bishop and author of the Confessions and The City of God. He describes two cities formed by two loves, and treats peace as the tranquillity of order.
voice: I ask which love is forming this people, because a people is known by what it loves.

works.title: The City of God
works.note: Project Gutenberg, Dods translation, volume II

entries.claim: Two cities have been formed by two loves: the earthly by the love of self, even to the contempt of God; the heavenly by the love of God, even to the contempt of self.
entries.bears: A common life is already a moral fact. It is gathered by what the people love.
entries.modern: Two cities have been formed by two loves: the earthly by the love of self, even to the contempt of God; the heavenly by the love of God, even to the contempt of self. A common life is already a moral fact. It is gathered by what the people love.

entries.claim: Peace is the tranquillity of order. The peace of a city is the ordered agreement of citizens.
entries.bears: Order is not mere quiet. It is a right arrangement.
entries.modern: Peace is the tranquillity of order. The peace of a city is the ordered agreement of citizens. Order is not mere quiet.

entries.claim: The earthly city desires earthly peace for the sake of enjoying earthly goods, and it makes war in order to attain that peace.
entries.bears: Even a worldly peace is an agreement about goods, not the absence of a moral question.
entries.modern: The earthly city desires earthly peace for the sake of enjoying earthly goods, and it makes war in order to attain that peace. Even a worldly peace is an agreement about goods, not the absence of a moral question.

entries.claim: A people is a multitude of reasonable beings bound together by a common agreement as to the objects of their love. To know a people, observe what it loves.
entries.bears: Where there is no shared love, there is not yet a people, only a crowd.
entries.modern: A people is a multitude of reasonable beings bound together by a common agreement as to the objects of their love. To know a people, observe what it loves. Where there is no shared love, there is not yet a people, only a crowd.

entries.claim: Thou madest us for Thyself, and our heart is restless, until it repose in Thee.
entries.bears: A shared restlessness, in this opening, is already aimed at God.
entries.modern: You madest us for Thyself, and our heart is restless, until it repose in You. A shared restlessness, in this opening, is already aimed at God.

entries.claim: If bodies please thee, praise God on occasion of them, and turn back thy love upon their Maker; lest in these things which please thee, thou displease.
entries.loc: On the love of created things
entries.bears: What is beautiful is not refused. The love is sent on to the maker.
entries.modern: If bodies please you, praise God on occasion of them, and turn back your love upon their Maker; lest in these things which please you, you displease. What is beautiful is not refused. The love is sent on to the maker.

entries.claim: For I had not known or learned that neither was evil a substance, nor our soul that chief and unchangeable good.
entries.bears: He refuses both a substance called evil and a soul that would be the highest good.
